## Natural history notes

A shrubby beard lichen characterized by pale gray-green, branching, hair-like strands that form bushy tufts on bark and branches. In Florida, it is found on trees and shrubs in humid forests, hammocks, swamps, pine flatwoods, parks, and other wooded habitats with good air flow and moisture. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air while using bark mainly as a surface for attachment rather than as food.
